summary: Use C# virtual dispatch for a statically known JavaScript class method override hierarchy when prototypes are stable.

target.notes: Emit the base method as virtual and the derived method as override so calls through a base-typed receiver still dispatch to the derived implementation.

semantics.js_lookup: ordinary property lookup starting at derived prototype
semantics.override: derived prototype property shadows base method

caveats: JavaScript can replace methods at runtime; C# virtual tables are static.

tests.name: derived override dispatch
tests.input: class B { m(){ return 1; } } class D extends B { m(){ return 2; } } const x=new D(); console.log(x.m());
tests.expected_csharp: public class B { public virtual double m()=>1d; } public class D:B { public override double m()=>2d; }

tests.name: edge: prototype replacement excludes native virtual dispatch
tests.input: class B { m(){return 1;} } class D extends B {} D.prototype.m=function(){return 3}; console.log(new D().m());
tests.expected_behavior: prints 3; static C# vtable emission alone is not sufficient if prototype mutation is allowed
